meta.title: Form Engine
meta.description: A form orchestration engine that manages multi-step or single-step form flow. Brings your own validation, fields, and state via react-hook-form and zod. The engine owns the steps — you own everything inside them.

blocks.content: A three-step account creation form. Step 1 and 2 have zod validation. Step 3 (billing) is optional and can be skipped.

The form engine owns exactly one thing: flow. It tracks which step is active, validates before advancing, and calls your onSubmit when done. Everything else — field values, validation schemas, error messages — belongs to react-hook-form and zod.

blocks.title: The engine never touches your fields
blocks.content: The engine calls validate() on each step before advancing. You wire validate() to form.trigger() from react-hook-form. That's the entire integration surface — one function that returns a boolean.
Use FormEngine for the batteries-included experience. It renders progress dots, step title, fields, and navigation buttons automatically.
Use createZodPlugin to add per-step zod validation. Pass a map of step index to schema. The plugin blocks navigation if the schema fails.
Field-level error messages from zod are displayed automatically below each field via react-hook-form. No extra wiring needed.
Plugins are the primary extension point. They hook into every lifecycle event — mount, step change, field change, validate, submit. Multiple plugins can be combined.
You can also write your own plugin inline.
Pass mode: "single" and a single step to use the engine as a regular form. The progress indicator is hidden and the Submit button appears immediately.
Use FormEngineRoot for full layout control. Compose the pieces yourself — progress, step meta, canvas, and navigation can be placed anywhere.
